chunk_findings.detail:
The refusal message instructs the user to fix a closed-unmerged back-merge by re-opening the request: `... re-open it or merge production into {into} yourself.` But once the closed state is recorded, the record's state is `"closed"`, and `_sync_back_merges` only ever iterates records whose recorded state is `"open"`:

```python
for rec in [r for r in _state(log).back_merges.values() if r["state"] == "open"]:
```

Concrete failure: (1) a hotfix merges, `_back_merge` opens `production -> develop` PR #10 and records `state="open"`; (2) #10 is closed unmerged, so a later `pr sync` logs `backmerge.recorded` with `state="closed"` and emits the refusal telling the user to re-open it; (3) the user follows that advice, re-opens #10 and merges it; (4) every subsequent `pr sync` filters on the *recorded* state, which is still `"closed"`, so #10 is never polled again — `forge.view(#10)` is never called, no `Change(..., "merged into develop", ...)` is ever emitted, and `pr status` keeps reporting the back-merge as closed even though develop now has the fix. `_back_merge` cannot rescue this either, since it is only reached at the moment the item's own PR merges and the item is no longer in REVIEW. So the one remediation the code itself suggests is guaranteed to leave the back-merge permanently untracked (the recorded "open" set is the only thing polled), which contradicts the stated goal of re-asking "until it lands".

chunk_findings.detail: `_h_back_merge_recorded` builds the tracked record entirely from the current event's data, defaulting `into`, `number`, `url`, `forge` and `state` to `""`, and derives the map key from `d["into"]`. The record's own documented contract (and the README, and `pr status`'s consumers) says `state` is one of `open | merged | closed`; nothing in the event forces that, so an initial `backmerge.recorded` event shaped like `{"into": "develop", "number": 7, "url": "...", "forge": "gh"}` (a freshly recorded request is by definition open, so the emitter has no reason to send `state`) stores `"state": ""`, and `pr status` reports a back-merge in a state that no consumer can classify as open vs. merged vs. closed. The same construction makes updates destructive: a later `backmerge.recorded` event for the same item that carries only the new `state` (the natural way to record "merged"/"closed", which the feature needs to stop re-asking) computes `into=""`, writes a *second* entry keyed `"<item>>"` with empty `number`/`url`/`forge`, and leaves the original open record untouched — so the merge/close is never reflected and `pr sync` keeps re-asking a request that is already resolved. The handler needs to merge into any existing entry (or require/validate `into` and default `state` to `"open"`) rather than overwrite from partial data.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/model.py:_h_back_merge_recorded

chunk_findings.detail: The gate in `sync` was changed to `if not waiting and not st.pending_releases and not open_back: return rep`, i.e. it now deliberately falls through when the only outstanding thing is an open back-merge — but in everything shown, `sync` has no call to `_sync_back_merges` (the new function is only *defined*; the waiting loop and the rest of `sync` are unchanged in this diff). Concrete case: item A's hotfix PR was detected merged in an earlier run, so `_back_merge` recorded `backmerge.recorded` with `state="open"` and PR #10; A is no longer in REVIEW and there are no pending releases. On the next `pr sync`, `waiting` is empty but `open_back` contains A's record, so the early return is skipped, `FG.detect` runs, the (empty) `for it in waiting` loop does nothing, and `sync` returns an empty `SyncReport`. PR #10 is never re-asked, so when it is later merged no `Change(item, "back_merge", "merged into develop")` is ever reported, and if it is closed unmerged the loud refusal never fires — exactly the behavior the intent claims ("every later pr sync re-asks until merged or closed"). The gate change is inert without that call; if the call lives in a part of the diff not shown here, please disregard, but as presented `_sync_back_merges` is dead code.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/flow.py — `sync` never invokes `_sync_back_merges`

chunk_findings.detail: `open_back = [r for r in st.back_merges.values() if r["state"] == "open"]` is computed over *all* records, while `waiting` is filtered by `(not only or it.id == only)` and `_sync_back_merges` later skips records with `rec["item"] != only`. So for `pr sync <X>` where X has nothing left to do (not in REVIEW, no pending release, no open back-merge of its own) but some other item Y still has an open back-merge, the early return no longer triggers and `sync` calls `FG.detect`. Previously such an invocation was a clean no-op; now it touches the forge for work it will then skip, and if detection fails (forge unreachable) the command surfaces an unavailable/refused error for a sync that previously succeeded silently. The fast-path condition should be computed from the `only`-filtered set (or `_sync_back_merges` should be the sole determinant).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/flow.py — `open_back` bypasses the `only` filter

chunk_findings.detail: The new condition reads the state of every back‑merge record with a hard subscript, `r["state"]`, yet this same change's own test `test_a_record_without_a_state_is_open` establishes that records are allowed to have *no* state: it appends exactly the payload a freshly opened back‑merge leaves behind (`{"into", "number", "url", "forge"}`, no `state`) and asserts the missing state means "open". That default is exercised only through `pr status` (which is what the test inspects), not through the projection that `next` reads. If the "open" default is applied when rendering the status rows rather than when `st.back_merges` is built, then the very first turn taken while a hotfix back‑merge is open — i.e. the scenario this change is for — raises `KeyError: 'state'` before `next` can sync anything, and `test_next_keeps_syncing_while_a_back_merge_is_open` would crash on its call to `next` instead of reaching its assertions. The condition should be `r.get("state") == "open"`, or the "open" default must be materialised in the projection so that both `pr status` and `next` see it.

chunk_findings.detail: `_h_back_merge_recorded` builds the tracked record entirely from the current event's data, defaulting `into`, `number`, `url`, `forge` and `state` to `""`, and derives the map key from `d["into"]`. The record's own documented contract (and the README, and `pr status`'s consumers) says `state` is one of `open | merged | closed`; nothing in the event forces that, so an initial `backmerge.recorded` event shaped like `{"into": "develop", "number": 7, "url": "...", "forge": "gh"}` (a freshly recorded request is by definition open, so the emitter has no reason to send `state`) stores `"state": ""`, and `pr status` reports a back-merge in a state that no consumer can classify as open vs. merged vs. closed. The same construction makes updates destructive: a later `backmerge.recorded` event for the same item that carries only the new `state` (the natural way to record "merged"/"closed", which the feature needs to stop re-asking) computes `into=""`, writes a *second* entry keyed `"<item>>"` with empty `number`/`url`/`forge`, and leaves the original open record untouched — so the merge/close is never reflected and `pr sync` keeps re-asking a request that is already resolved. The handler needs to merge into any existing entry (or require/validate `into` and default `state` to `"open"`) rather than overwrite from partial data.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/model.py:_h_back_merge_recorded

chunk_findings.detail: The gate in `sync` was changed to `if not waiting and not st.pending_releases and not open_back: return rep`, i.e. it now deliberately falls through when the only outstanding thing is an open back-merge — but in everything shown, `sync` has no call to `_sync_back_merges` (the new function is only *defined*; the waiting loop and the rest of `sync` are unchanged in this diff). Concrete case: item A's hotfix PR was detected merged in an earlier run, so `_back_merge` recorded `backmerge.recorded` with `state="open"` and PR #10; A is no longer in REVIEW and there are no pending releases. On the next `pr sync`, `waiting` is empty but `open_back` contains A's record, so the early return is skipped, `FG.detect` runs, the (empty) `for it in waiting` loop does nothing, and `sync` returns an empty `SyncReport`. PR #10 is never re-asked, so when it is later merged no `Change(item, "back_merge", "merged into develop")` is ever reported, and if it is closed unmerged the loud refusal never fires — exactly the behavior the intent claims ("every later pr sync re-asks until merged or closed"). The gate change is inert without that call; if the call lives in a part of the diff not shown here, please disregard, but as presented `_sync_back_merges` is dead code.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/flow.py — `sync` never invokes `_sync_back_merges`

chunk_findings.detail: `open_back = [r for r in st.back_merges.values() if r["state"] == "open"]` is computed over *all* records, while `waiting` is filtered by `(not only or it.id == only)` and `_sync_back_merges` later skips records with `rec["item"] != only`. So for `pr sync <X>` where X has nothing left to do (not in REVIEW, no pending release, no open back-merge of its own) but some other item Y still has an open back-merge, the early return no longer triggers and `sync` calls `FG.detect`. Previously such an invocation was a clean no-op; now it touches the forge for work it will then skip, and if detection fails (forge unreachable) the command surfaces an unavailable/refused error for a sync that previously succeeded silently. The fast-path condition should be computed from the `only`-filtered set (or `_sync_back_merges` should be the sole determinant).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/flow.py — `open_back` bypasses the `only` filter
